title: Apricot custard tart
subtitle: baked egg custard tart with fresh apricots
excerpt: An apricot custard tart sets a rich vanilla custard in a buttery short pastry case, with halved fresh apricots nestled into the filling before baking. The apricots soften in the oven and their juices bleed slightly into the custard, creating a jammy-edged fruit against the set cream. It's best eaten warm or at room temperature; the custard firms as it cools but remains silky.
sourceNotes: Custard tarts filled with seasonal fruit are a standard of French and British pâtisserie. The French version, tarte à la crème aux abricots, layers frangipane or pastry cream with fresh apricots in a blind-baked shell; the British version, more commonly, pours a baked custard directly into the shell with the fruit sitting in it. Both traditions appear in domestic cookery books from at least the late 19th century. Fresh apricots are brief in season, they're at their best for about six weeks in summer, and this tart is one of the simplest ways to make use of them.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten on the day it's made; the pastry softens overnight.
recipe.temperatureNote: for baking the custard; the oven must not be hotter or the custard will bubble and curdle

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: low oven for the custard fill (160°C conventional or 140°C fan); blind bake the case first at 190°C

content.text: An apricot custard tart is a summer tart at its simplest: good buttery pastry, silky vanilla custard, and ripe apricots. The apricots go in raw and soften as the custard sets. The custard bakes at 160°C, lower than you might expect, because a hotter oven makes it bubble and separate.
Make and blind bake the pastry case

Rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and cold water and bring together into a dough. Wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Roll out to 3 mm thick and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Trim the edges, prick the base, and refrigerate for 20 minutes. Preheat the oven to 190°C conventional. Line the pastry with parchment, fill with baking beans, and blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and bake for a further 10 minutes until the base is dry and pale gold.
Pour in the custard and add the apricots

Reduce the oven to 160°C conventional (140°C fan). Whisk together the cream, milk, egg yolks, whole egg, sugar, and vanilla until combined but not frothy. Place the tart tin on a baking sheet. Arrange the apricot halves cut-side up in the pastry case. Pour the custard around them to fill the case to just below the rim. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the custard is set with a faint wobble in the centre and the apricots are tender. Cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.
